nodes.summary: The set of even natural numbers has natural density $1/2$.
nodes.title: Natural density of the even numbers

nodes.summary: Every finite set of natural numbers has natural density $0$.
nodes.title: Finite sets have natural density zero

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, let $S, A \subseteq \beta$ and $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$, and write $\beta_{\lt b} = \{x \in \beta \mid x < b\}$. The set $S$ has density $\alpha$ relative to $A$ if the partial density $\lvert S \cap A \cap \beta_{\lt b} \rvert / \lvert A \cap \beta_{\lt b} \rvert$, taken to be $0$ when the denominator is $0$, tends to $\alpha$ as…
nodes.title: Density of a set

nodes.summary: A set $S$ of integers has two-sided natural density $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$ if $\lvert S \cap [-N, N] \rvert / (2N + 1)$ tends to $\alpha$ as the natural number $N$ tends to infinity, where $[-N, N]$ is the set of integers $m$ with $-N \le m \le N$.
nodes.title: Two-sided natural density

nodes.summary: A set $A$ of natural numbers has logarithmic density $d \in \mathbb{R}$ if $\frac{1}{\log n} \sum_{k \in A,\, k \le n} \frac{1}{k}$ tends to $d$ as $n \to \infty$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm, the term $1/k$ for $k = 0$ is taken to be $0$, and the whole expression is taken to be $0$ when $\log n = 0$.
nodes.title: Logarithmic density

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, and let $S, A \subseteq \beta$. The set $S$ has positive density relative to $A$ if there is a real number $\alpha > 0$ such that $S$ has density $\alpha$ relative to $A$. By default $A = \beta$.
nodes.title: Positive density

nodes.summary: If a set $S$ of natural numbers has natural density $\alpha$ with $\alpha \neq 0$, then $S$ is infinite.
nodes.title: Sets of nonzero natural density are infinite

nodes.summary: For a set $S$ of integers and a natural number $N$, the two-sided partial natural density of $S$ at $N$ is $\lvert S \cap [-N, N] \rvert / (2N + 1)$, where $[-N, N]$ is the set of integers $m$ with $-N \le m \le N$.
nodes.title: Two-sided partial density

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, and let $S, A \subseteq \beta$. The lower density of $S$ relative to $A$ is the limit inferior, as $b \to \infty$ in $\beta$, of the partial densities of $S$ relative to $A$ at $b$. By default $A = \beta$.
nodes.title: Lower density

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, let $S, A \subseteq \beta$ and $b \in \beta$, and write $A_{\lt b} = \{x \in A \mid x < b\}$. The partial density of $S$ relative to $A$ at $b$ is the proportion $\lvert S \cap A_{\lt b} \rvert / \lvert A_{\lt b} \rvert$ of elements of $A_{\lt b}$ that lie in $S$, taken to be $0$ when $A_{\lt b}$ is empty. By default $A = \beta$.
nodes.title: Partial density

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a partial order with a least element and at least two elements, in which every closed interval $[a, b]$ is finite. Then the set of all elements of $\beta$ has density $1$ (relative to all of $\beta$).
nodes.title: The whole order has density one

nodes.summary: Let $\beta$ be a preorder in which every set $\{x \in \beta \mid x \le b\}$ is finite, and let $S, A \subseteq \beta$. The upper density of $S$ relative to $A$ is the limit superior, as $b \to \infty$ in $\beta$, of the partial densities of $S$ relative to $A$ at $b$. By default $A = \beta$.
nodes.title: Upper density

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
